From the existing project root, with Node.js 18+ and pnpm available, the future setup sequence is:

```sh
pnpm add -D @tgcloud/cli
pnpm exec tgcloud init
```

The first command installs a local development dependency and updates dependency files. The second scaffolds `tgcloud/`, configuration, documentation, and local state while preserving existing files. Keep `web/` in place; do not create another frontend or bot. Review generated files and any added package scripts before proceeding.

If you want Telegram to host the frontend later, set the root `tgcloud.jsonc` configuration to include:

```json
{ "static": { "source": "web/dist" } }
```

That path is relative to the project root. Linking alone does not require building or publishing the frontend.

To link the already-created Serverless bot later:

```sh
pnpm exec tgcloud login
```

In your local interactive terminal, enter the CLI access token from BotFather → your existing bot → Serverless → CLI Access. This is separate from the Bot API token. Never send it in chat. Login contacts Telegram and saves it in `.tgcloud/credentials`; keep `.tgcloud/` ignored.

Finish with offline `pnpm exec tgcloud status`. Setup/linking does not deploy code or migrate data.

[Official setup documentation](https://core.telegram.org/bots/serverless#1-create-a-project)
